text.p: Dutch-owned German consumer electronics group Grundig said on Wednesday losses this year would be in line with expectations after the company embarked on a major restructuring programme.

Chief executive Pieter van der Wahl said in a statement the results would be "unsatisfactory, as expected". Earlier, weekly financial magazine Capital said net losses would hit 250 million marks in 1996.
A loss for 1996 "is no surprise," van der Wal said, adding that his restructuring plan would begin to have an impact early next year.
The chief exeuctive's statement did not mean Grundig would generate a profit in 1997, a company spokesman said. He would not say when the company expected to return to black figures.
Grundig will not be able to count on financial help from Philips after their controlling agreement runs out at the end of this year.

Capital reported Grundig's 1996 sales would remain level at 3.5 billion marks. The firm would suffer an operating loss of 160 million marks, and would incur 90 million marks in unplanned warranty costs, the magazine wrote.
Grundig plans to move from its Fuerth headquarters to a smaller location near Nuremberg, the spokesman said. The restructuring program has eliminated about 3,000.
